title: Photomultiplier dynode cascade pre-amplifier for femtofarad cells
idea: Borrow the photomultiplier's dynode chain: the bitline feeds a stack of three gated-diode charge amplifiers, each transferring and multiplying the packet (~3x per stage by collapsing a gate-boosted capacitance) before the latch fires. A 1.5 fF cell then looks like a ~20 fF cell to the latch.
why: Capacitor charge wall: Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~1.5 fF, so pillar AR goes from ~70:1 to ~20:1, or 3D tiers can use small lateral caps. Costs ~5% SA area.

title: Lock-in chopper sense amp doubles cells per bitline
idea: As in a lock-in amplifier, cross-switches chop bitline vs reference at ~4 GHz during signal development; the preamp works in the modulated band and a demodulator feeds the latch, so SA offset and 1/f noise fall outside the signal band. Resolvable signal drops from ~80 mV to ~25 mV.
why: Periphery area: 1024 instead of 512 cells per bitline halves the SA stripes (~10% of die); or the same margin with ~3x smaller Cs.

title: HDD PRML joint detection replaces bitline shielding and twisting
idea: Treat bitline-to-bitline coupling as intersymbol interference, as an HDD read channel does: sample 8 adjacent bitlines with two-level comparators, run a 4-state Viterbi detector in the column path that decides all 8 jointly, then restore. Shield lines, twist regions and folded layouts are dropped for minimum-pitch open bitlines.
why: Periphery/density: removes twist and shield overhead (~5-8% of array plus SA stripe) and tolerates 2x coupling, making 4F2 open-bitline cells viable without a noise penalty.

title: CCD bucket-brigade shifts row charge to one edge sense node
idea: Like a CCD image sensor, each mat's bitlines become buried-channel charge-transfer registers: an activated row dumps its packets into the channel, and clock phases march them to one high-gain floating-diffusion amplifier at the mat edge, read serially and restored through a write-back register. One sense chain serves 16 columns.
why: Periphery area: SA count falls 16x (SA stripes ~20% of die to ~3%); serial readout matches HBM bursts, and only burst bits are moved, which cuts overfetch.

title: Image-sensor single-slope ramp ADC reads two bits per cell
idea: Copy the CMOS image sensor's column ADC: one global ramp generator per bank plus a 6-transistor comparator and 2-bit counter latch per bitline turn the developed bitline voltage into one of 4 levels; restore writes back one of 4 voltages from shared DAC rails.
why: Cost per bit: 2 bits/cell is ~1.8x bits per wafer for ~12% more SA area; the ramp is shared, so periphery per bit falls.

title: Display gate-on-array IGZO wordline drivers stacked above the array
idea: LCD makers moved gate drivers onto the glass as thin-film shift registers (gate-on-array). Do the same: build sub-wordline drivers and local row-decode NAND as IGZO TFT circuits in the BEOL directly over the cell array, leaving only global predecode in silicon.
why: Periphery area: sub-wordline driver stripes (~10-12% of die) go to near zero, for ~10% more bits per wafer, if IGZO TFTs tolerate the 3 V wordline swing.

title: Solar MPPT perturb-and-observe tracking of sense references
idea: Like a solar inverter hunting the maximum power point, each mat controller nudges its sense reference/precharge level by +/-5 mV on ECC-protected reads and keeps whichever direction lowers the corrected-bit count, so the reference follows temperature, aging and 1-vs-0 retention asymmetry.
why: Refresh: a centred reference reads decaying '1' cells correctly for longer, roughly doubling the refresh interval (refresh energy -50%, bandwidth +5-10%).

title: Spiking-neuron voltage-to-delay time-domain sensing
idea: Like an integrate-and-fire neuron, the developed bitline voltage sets the discharge current of a small node, turning a 30 mV difference into a ~20 ps race; a tiny SR-latch arbiter decides whether bitline or reference fires first, with digital delay trims absorbing mismatch.
why: Periphery area: a digital-style comparator scales with logic nodes and is ~2x smaller than large matched analog SA transistors.

title: Battery active balancing recycles bitline charge between subarrays
idea: Like a BMS shuttling charge from full cells to empty ones, a switched flying-capacitor bus links subarrays: when subarray A equalizes its full-swing bitlines, its surplus charge is dumped into subarray B, which is mid-restore. About 40% of restore charge is recycled from the previous activation.
why: Energy per bit/voltage floor: bitline CV2 dominates activation; activate energy falls ~30-40%, as does charge-pump load.

title: Core-memory coincident selection with threshold-switch row drivers
idea: Revive magnetic core memory's coincident-current trick: each local wordline driver is gated by a two-terminal ovonic threshold switch fed by one X and one Y predecode line, each at half threshold. Only the row where both are active fires its driver, replacing NAND decode trees.
why: Periphery area: row-decoder transistor count falls ~4x (decoders ~8-10% of die to ~3%); the OTS is BEOL-compatible.

title: Radar time-of-flight addressing with counter-propagating pulses
idea: Like a phased array placing energy where waves meet, launch two short pulses into opposite ends of a row-select transmission line; their launch delay sets where they overlap, and only there does the summed amplitude exceed the row-driver threshold. A 512-row decoder becomes two pulse generators and a digital delay.
why: Periphery area: decoders shrink ~10x, if ~10 ps on-die timing and dispersion can be controlled.

title: District-heating supply of wordline high voltage from base die
idea: Like a district heating plant replacing a boiler in every house, generate VPP (~3 V) and negative back-bias in one efficient inductive or switched-capacitor converter on the HBM base die or DIMM PMIC, and deliver them to every core die through dedicated TSVs/pads instead of many small on-die charge pumps.
why: Periphery area (~5-7% of die in pumps and pump caps) and energy: pump efficiency rises from ~30% to ~85%, halving wordline supply energy.

title: Grid capacitor banks: dummy cell capacitors become pumps and decap
idea: Like a utility's capacitor bank, gang the edge/dummy rows of the cell array, whose high-AR capacitors are already built (~50 fF/um2), in parallel as charge-pump flying capacitors and on-die decoupling, replacing large planar MOS capacitors in the periphery.
why: Periphery area: MOS pump and decap area (~3-5% of die) shrinks ~10x by borrowing the densest capacitor on the chip.

title: HDD servo wedges: embedded calibration rows retrim sense amps
idea: Like servo bursts written between data sectors on a disk, every mat holds a few known-pattern calibration rows; during refresh slots each SA reads them and steps a per-SA 4-bit trim capacitor until its offset is nulled, continuously in the background.
why: Periphery area: SA transistors can be near minimum size, since trim absorbs offset, shrinking the SA stripe ~30-40% and tolerating more Vt variation at small F.

title: Battery coulomb-counting: dual-threshold reads flag weakening rows
idea: Like a battery gauge estimating health on every cycle, each SA gets a second small comparator at a raised '1' threshold; normal reads flag cells that have lost >40% of charge, and the row goes into a per-bank weak-row table refreshed at 4x while all other rows refresh at 1/4 rate.
why: Refresh (46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power): ~60-70% fewer refreshes, driven by live in-field retention data instead of one-time profiling.

title: Insurance pool: hashed global spare columns replace per-mat redundancy
idea: Like insurers pooling risk instead of every household holding reserves, remove the redundant columns from each subarray and give each bank a shared pool of spare column segments addressed by a small CAM keyed on (subarray, column), mapped in at the column path.
why: Periphery overhead: redundancy and fuse area (~3-6% of die) roughly halves, because statistical multiplexing needs ~5x fewer spares for the same yield.

title: Fiber-optic EDFA-style in-line repeaters along long bitlines
idea: Like optical amplifiers spaced along long-haul fiber, insert a tiny IGZO TFT preamp/isolation switch in the BEOL every 128 cells, buffering each local segment's signal onto a global bitline, so one silicon SA serves an 8x longer bitline.
why: Periphery area: SA stripes shrink ~4-8x (~15-20% of die to ~4%); segmenting also cuts bitline C, raising signal per fF of Cs.

title: Regenerative braking for wordlines via stepwise energy recovery
idea: Like an EV recovering energy while braking, discharge each 3 V wordline down a 5-step on-die capacitor ladder (stepwise adiabatic charging) instead of to ground, and charge the next wordline back up the same ladder.
why: Voltage floor/energy: wordline CV2 loss at ~3 V falls ~60-70% (N-step charging dissipates ~1/N), with less charge-pump load.

title: Radio aperture synthesis: twin mini-cells summed on one bitline
idea: Like an interferometer combining small dishes into one big aperture, store each bit in two half-size capacitors on different tiers/wordlines that fire together onto one bitline; their charges add, so each capacitor needs only ~2.5 fF.
why: 3D DRAM capacitor blocker: lateral capacitors need half the charge, at the cost of 2x cells, which are cheap in 3D; this may lower the 26-tier break-even.

title: Drip-irrigation valves: column-gated local wordlines stop overfetch
idea: Like drip lines watering only the plants that need it, split each 8 kb row into 32 segments whose local wordline is gated by a BEOL vertical select transistor driven from the column address, so an activate opens only the 256 bits being read.
why: Overfetch/destructive read (~5.9 pJ per useful bit, 128x overfetch): random-access activate energy falls ~10-20x, and row-hammer exposure falls too.

title: Roundabout traffic: self-timed completion detection per mat
idea: Like a roundabout letting cars go as soon as the way is clear instead of waiting for a fixed signal cycle, each SA latch drives a dual-rail done signal, and a per-mat completion tree releases column access when that mat's slowest SA resolves, not after the chip's worst-case tRCD.
why: Latency/bandwidth: average tRCD falls ~25-35% by reclaiming PVT guard-bands.

title: LTPS display demux: one sense amp serves four bitlines
idea: Like the 1:3 demultiplexers that let one display source driver feed several columns, bitlines develop in parallel and hold their signal on their own capacitance while a BEOL switch tree steps one SA across four bitlines in ~1 ns slots, restoring each before moving on.
why: Periphery area: SA count falls 4x (SA stripe ~15% to ~5% of die) for ~+3 ns tRAS; nanosecond holding fits the leakage budget.

title: Options trading: speculative early latch with cancellable confirmation
idea: Like buying an option, a small fast SA latches at ~40% signal development and ships data early; the main SA finishes at full development and, on the rare disagreement, sends a cancel/replay token on the data bus, like exercising the option.
why: Latency: ~30% faster tRCD on most reads, with replays rare (<1e-4) when references are centred.

title: Xerographic dry printing of periphery power and global routing
idea: Xerography means 'dry writing': image the periphery's relaxed-pitch (>=300 nm) global/power metal pattern onto a charged photoconductive transfer drum, pick up copper-nanoparticle 'toner' electrostatically, transfer it to the wafer and laser-sinter in forming gas. No resist, plating bath, CMP or post-CMP clean.
why: Water: the top 3-4 periphery metal layers (damascene plating, CMP and scrub rinses) need ~10x less UPW, and plating/CMP chemical waste disappears. Resolution and adhesion are the risks.

title: Liquid-CO2 garment dry-cleaning for periphery post-etch residue
idea: Dry cleaners replaced perchloroethylene with liquid CO2. Clean every periphery post-etch and post-ash step with supercritical CO2 plus 1-3% alcohol/amine cosolvent in a pressure chamber that recaptures >95% of the CO2, keeping one short single-wafer UPW rinse only before the gate.
why: Water: ~30-40 periphery residue cleans each drop from ~10-20 L UPW per wafer to near zero, ~10x less for the module; relaxed periphery pitch makes scCO2 penetration easy.

title: Instant-photography dry resist and dry develop for periphery litho
idea: Like Polaroid replacing the wet darkroom, vapor-deposit a metal-oxide photoresist, expose, develop it in a plasma/thermal gas step and strip it dry on every periphery-only mask (implant blocks, contacts, metals), so these layers never touch developer, rinse or wet strip.
why: Water: track develop/rinse and post-implant wet strips (~15-25 L UPW per layer) fall ~10x on periphery layers; resist solvent supply chains shrink too.

title: Cloud erasure coding lets periphery fabs skip particle cleans
idea: Backblaze runs cheap consumer disks reliably by erasure-coding across them. Group each bank's 16 subarrays with 2 parity subarrays and an on-die Reed-Solomon reconstruct engine in the column path, so a particle-killed subarray is rebuilt on the fly, and the fab removes ~80% of inter-step particle scrubs and megasonic rinses.
why: Water: ~10x higher killer-defect density is tolerated, so particle-removal rinses, a top UPW user, fall ~5-10x at constant yield; parity costs ~12% array area.

title: Drywall prefab: array wafers plus dry-bonded periphery chiplets
idea: Construction cut on-site water by moving from wet plaster to factory drywall. Keep only pitch-matched SAs on the array wafer and move the non-pitch-matched periphery (pumps, global decode, control, DLL, I/O) to 40 nm logic chiplets, bonded fluxless with formic-acid-vapor reflow and plasma activation, both dry steps.
why: Water: the array wafer skips the high-metal-count logic module, and the chiplets use few wet steps on ~1/3 the area, so water for that periphery falls ~10x; it also takes periphery off EUV.

title: Deep Space Network weak-signal sensing frees capacitors from wet mold-strip
idea: NASA hears Voyager's 20 W transmitter by building great receivers, not louder transmitters. Correlated double sampling (sample the bitline after equalize and after charge share, subtract on a capacitor pair) plus a low-noise preamp resolves ~15 mV, so cells can use a ~1.5 fF, ~15:1 dry-etched capacitor instead of a 70:1 cylinder that needs a wet HF mold-oxide strip and many high-AR rinse/dry cycles.
why: Water and the capacitor wall: the mold strip, stiction-safe rinse/IPA dry and high-AR cleans, among DRAM's most UPW-hungry steps, fall ~10x; capacitor-module steps fall ~40%.

title: Vinyl record pressing: nanoimprint all periphery-only layers
idea: Like pressing vinyl from a master stamper, pattern periphery-only layers (implant blocks, periphery contacts, metals at >=40 nm half-pitch) by jet-and-flash nanoimprint: drop-dispensed UV resist, imprint, cure, and descum the residual layer by plasma. No wet develop, no BARC rinse, no EUV.
why: Water: each periphery litho module loses its develop/rinse (~10x less UPW per layer); litho capital per periphery layer is ~3-5x lower.

title: Sculptor carving: subtractive dry-etched ruthenium/molybdenum periphery wiring
idea: Damascene copper is casting: pour into a mold, then grind and wash (CMP). Carve instead, like a sculptor: blanket-deposit Ru or Mo, pattern, and plasma-etch the periphery's local/intermediate wiring and contacts, then gap-fill with flowable low-k. No barrier, plating, CMP or post-CMP scrub.
why: Water: CMP plus post-CMP cleans, among the biggest UPW users per layer, fall ~10x on periphery metal levels; Mo contacts (U.S.-mined) also replace tungsten, easing the China-80% chokepoint.

title: Passive-house memory: tunnel-FET latch sensing at 0.35 V
idea: Passive houses skip HVAC by cutting the heat load at the source. Run the array at VARY 0.35 V and sense with a cross-coupled tunnel-FET latch (steep <40 mV/dec slope keeps gain at low voltage), cutting bitline CV2 ~8x so modules stay within air-cooling heat flux and racks need no evaporative cooling for memory power.
why: Lifecycle water/energy: DRAM is 20-30% of server power; ~8x less array energy plus air cooling cuts the evaporated cooling water attributable to memory (~1-2 L/kWh) ~10x and breaks the voltage floor.

title: Hospital plasma sterilization: radical-based pre-gate clean for periphery
idea: Hospitals swapped steam autoclaves for hydrogen-peroxide plasma sterilizers. Replace the RCA wet sequence before the periphery high-k/metal-gate stack with remote hydrogen-radical organic/metal removal plus anhydrous HF/alcohol vapor oxide etch in one vacuum chamber.
why: Water: RCA SC1/SC2/HF with cascaded rinses (~50-100 L UPW per full clean) is the classic water hog; the dry radical sequence cuts ~10x across the ~4-6 periphery pre-gate/pre-diffusion cleans.

title: Monument laser cleaning: shock-wave particle removal before periphery contacts
idea: Conservators clean cathedral stone with pulsed lasers and no water. A nanosecond laser flash-heats the wafer surface so thermal expansion and the gas-film shock wave lift particles from periphery contact/via openings, and a nitrogen cross-flow sweeps them into an exhaust, replacing megasonic DI-water scrubs.
why: Water: periphery particle scrubs (~10-20 L UPW each) fall ~10x, and dry removal has no capillary pattern-collapse risk.

title: Vacuum canning: no-air-break integration of periphery gate and contacts
idea: Canned food needs no preservatives because it never meets air. Run the periphery gate stack (interface, high-k, metal, cap) and the contact module (etch, liner, fill) each in one vacuum cluster with in-situ dry cleans, so wafers never grow native oxide or pick up airborne contamination, and queue-time wet re-cleans disappear.
why: Water: ~10-15 inter-step wet cleans per periphery flow are removed (~10x less water in those modules), along with queue-time scrap; cycle time also falls.

title: Solar epitaxial lift-off: periphery layer on a reused donor wafer
idea: High-efficiency III-V solar cells peel their thin active layer off a GaAs substrate that is reused many times. Grow the periphery CMOS device layer on a porous-silicon release layer, bond it to the array wafer, split it off, and re-epi the donor 10+ times instead of consuming a fresh prime wafer for the periphery tier.
why: Water and scarce resources: crystal-growth and wafering (slice, lap, polish, clean) water per periphery tier falls ~10x, and so does Spruce Pine quartz-crucible demand for that tier.

title: Tire retreading: CXL rehab buffer gives retired DRAM second life
idea: Truck fleets retread tires instead of buying new. Sell a CXL memory-expander buffer chip whose periphery profiles retired DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs in situ (per-row retention margin, weak-column sensing), applies per-region refresh rates and column remaps, and pools them as tier-2 memory under strong ECC, fed by hyperscaler decommissioning streams.
why: Water/supply: a reused GB avoids essentially all of its manufacturing water (>10x vs new) and adds supply with no fab; large volumes of retired DRAM are shredded today.

title: Camel-nose countercurrent cascade rinses for periphery wet benches
idea: A camel's nasal turbinates recover exhaled water by countercurrent exchange. Plumb periphery wet benches as 4-stage countercurrent cascades: fresh UPW enters only the final rinse and its overflow feeds the stage before, with inline resistivity/TOC sensors advancing wafers instead of timed overflow; periphery's relaxed contamination spec permits it.
why: Water: rinse water per periphery clean falls ~8-12x (efficiency compounds with stage count) with no new chemistry.

title: Charlieplexed wordline decode with bidirectional selector pairs
idea: Hobbyists drive N(N-1) LEDs from N pins by Charlieplexing with tri-state polarity. Hang each sub-wordline driver gate between an ordered pair of predecode lines through a polarity-sensitive diode-like BEOL selector, so 24 tri-state predecode lines address 552 drivers instead of a full NAND decoder per row.
why: Water via area: row-decode area falls ~10x (decoders ~8-10% of die to <1%), cutting the wafers, and hence the water, attributable to decoding ~10x; die area -8%.

title: Model T periphery: sense amps from the array transistor only
idea: Ford's Model T came in one colour to cut production steps. Design every pitch-matched periphery circuit (SAs, sub-wordline drivers, column switches) from the buried-channel array transistor plus one thick-oxide variant, using bootstrapped gates and NMOS-only latches with capacitive pull-up instead of a separate HKMG CMOS periphery module.
why: Water: deleting the periphery HKMG module (~8-12 masks, ~40 wet cleans and strips) cuts that module's water >10x and total fab water ~20%; mask and EUV counts fall too.

title: Telescope-mirror peel-off polymer: dry particle capture film
idea: Observatories clean mirrors with a peel-off polymer that cures around dust and lifts it away. Spin a strippable polymer onto periphery wafers after CMP or etch, let it encapsulate particles and residues, then peel it off with an adhesive roller tape in a dry module, leaving the surface clean.
why: Water: replaces post-CMP and pre-deposition brush/megasonic rinses in periphery modules (~10x less UPW per clean); the risk is complete release from trenches.

title: Palo Verde model: periphery chiplet fab running on reclaimed sewage
idea: Arizona's Palo Verde nuclear plant cools with treated municipal wastewater instead of freshwater. Site a U.S. periphery/logic-chiplet fab beside a city wastewater plant, take tertiary effluent as UPW feedstock, run zero-liquid-discharge with air-cooled chillers, and contract long-term effluent rights.
why: Water: freshwater withdrawal per wafer falls >10x (effluent replaces potable supply, ZLD recovers ~90%), easing Southwest permits and U.S. siting.

title: Stencil spray-paint: shadow-mask deposition of periphery pads and power
idea: Like a graffiti stencil, deposit the periphery's wide top-level features (pads, power straps, redistribution at >=2 um) through a reusable silicon-nitride MEMS stencil held in proximity during sputtering or evaporation. No resist, develop, strip or post-etch clean.
why: Water: top-metal/pad litho, etch and clean sequences (~30-50 L UPW per layer) fall ~10x, and those layers cost a fraction to pattern.

title: Mars electrodynamic dust shield built into the wafer chuck
idea: Mars and lunar solar panels shed dust with a traveling-wave field from embedded electrodes. Build interleaved 3-phase electrodes into the electrostatic chucks and load locks of periphery dry tools, hopping charged particles off the wafer into a vacuum trap between steps instead of sending wafers to scrubber rinses.
why: Water: post-step brush/spray scrubs in periphery modules (~5-10 L each) fall ~10x, and particles are caught before they become defects.

title: WaterSense label for chips: grants priced per liter per gigabyte
idea: EPA's WaterSense label made low-flow fixtures mainstream. Define an audited liters-per-GB metric and tie CHIPS-style grants, tax credits and federal procurement preference to tiers (top tier <=10% of the 2025 baseline), which rewards dry periphery flows, weak-signal sensing that simplifies capacitors, and wafer reuse.
why: Water/U.S. manufacturability: the 10x target becomes a funded design rule, pulling dry tools and periphery redesigns into U.S. fabs where water permits limit siting.

title: Apartment-tower shared lobby: one sense die serves eight array dies
idea: An apartment tower shares one lobby and elevator bank. Stack eight array-only dies whose short bitline segments drop through hybrid-bonded vertical vias into one shared sense/decode die, with a tier-select switch at each die's bitline foot so one die connects at a time.
why: Water/periphery: periphery wafers per bit fall ~8x and array dies need no CMOS module, so periphery-attributable water falls ~10x with no new chemistry; added via capacitance is the physics risk.
